note: Structured evidence for every external claim projected into docs/comparison.md, including the operation-level behaviour cells. Each record is immutable per observation: refreshing a claim ADDS a record (with its own observedAt) and the generator is pointed at the new id, rather than editing an existing one — so a superseded observation keeps its provenance and is allowed to sit here expired once it is no longer projected. Allowed primary-source origins are NOT declared here; they live in TRUSTED_PRIMARY_SOURCE_PREFIXES in scripts/lib/competitor-evidence.mjs so evidence cannot whitelist its own source. Validated and projected by that module (honua-io/honua-sdk-js#499 REQ-003/REQ-005/REQ-006, NFR-002).

headless-service-client.label: Headless service clients
headless-service-client.definition: Typed data/service clients that talk to geospatial services and hand results to a renderer they do not own. They ship no map engine, so their bytes are not comparable with a renderer's.

renderer-engine.label: Renderer engines
renderer-engine.definition: Map rendering engines (and their bundled format parsers). They draw maps; they do not provide a first-party typed client for service discovery, paging, edits, or capability negotiation.

renderer-sdk.label: Vendor-integrated renderer SDKs
renderer-sdk.definition: Renderer SDKs integrated with a vendor's styles, data, and application ecosystem. Specialized service APIs may live in separate packages, so the honest comparison is a complete application stack rather than a headless client alone.

hosted-application-sdk.label: Hosted map application SDKs
hosted-application-sdk.definition: Client SDKs that control maps, layers, interactions, authoring, and application UI hosted by a vendor platform. They compare directly on application workflow and developer experience, while persistence, rendering, and deployment remain platform-bound.

records.claim: Esri's own automated build metrics for its minimal @arcgis/core map samples report a 1.31–1.49 MB minified main bundle (0.36–0.42 MB gzip), 3.5–4.1 MB of JavaScript loaded at startup for a simple map view, and 8.3–10 MB of on-disk build output across roughly 300–740 files.
records.historicalReason: 4.30 is the last release line for which Esri published core-sample build metrics in jsapi-resources, and the product has since moved to a 5.x line. The figures therefore describe a superseded version and cannot stand in for a current measurement.
records.methodology: Esri's automated build-metrics harness over its minimal core-sample apps across the esbuild, Angular, React, Vue, Rollup and Webpack lanes; ranges span those lanes. Published as a CSV in Esri's jsapi-resources repository and cited here at a pinned commit.

metrics.label: JavaScript loaded at startup for a simple map view

records.comparability: Bundles a renderer, so the only category-correct counterpart is a headless client PLUS a renderer engine, never a headless client alone. The startup figure counts transferred JavaScript for a running sample; Honua's per-entrypoint numbers are static bundler output for an imported entrypoint. Those are different workloads under different harnesses: they may be reported side by side with this caveat, but not divided into a ratio.

records.claim: The current published @arcgis/core release line on the npm registry is 5.1.15, later than the 4.30 line for which Esri last published core-sample build metrics.
records.methodology: `npm view @arcgis/core version` against the public npm registry, which is the package's primary distribution channel.
records.comparability: Establishes only which release line is current. It carries no size or performance measurement and must not be used to imply one.

records.claim: ArcGIS REST JS is Esri's lightweight, modular REST client family for ArcGIS services. It provides no map runtime; it exposes ArcGIS service metadata, paging parameters, an output-spatial-reference parameter, and applyEdits, and its geocoding and routing packages address Esri's ArcGIS location services. It exposes no query-plan/explain surface and its request helpers are stateless.
records.methodology: Product scope and operation-level surface read from Esri's official ArcGIS REST JS documentation; the version line is the latest `@esri/arcgis-rest-request` published to the npm registry, read with `npm view`.
records.comparability: Same category as @honua/sdk-js (headless service client), so protocol and operation coverage compare directly. No bundle-size figure is claimed here, and none should be inferred: this repo has not measured it under the same harness as its own entrypoints.

paging.note: params exposed; caller drives the loop

records.claim: OpenLayers is a map rendering library that also ships format parsers (for example GeoJSON, EsriJSON, WFS/GML), tile/image sources, WMS/WMTS capabilities parsers, and built-in coordinate transforms. It provides no cross-protocol discovery contract, no service paging client, and no query-plan surface; WFS transactions are built as XML the caller sends.
records.methodology: Product scope and operation-level surface read from the official OpenLayers site and its API documentation; the version line is the latest `ol` published to the npm registry, read with `npm view`.
records.comparability: A renderer engine, not a headless service client. Its footprint depends heavily on which modules a consumer tree-shakes, so no single bundle number is quoted; the category-correct comparison is operation coverage of its first-party format/source modules.

records.claim: MapLibre GL JS is a map rendering engine. It renders sources a developer configures, in its own display projection, and exposes map teardown via `map.remove()`. It provides no service discovery, no feature paging, no edit transactions, no capability negotiation, and no query-plan surface.
records.methodology: Product scope and operation-level surface read from the official MapLibre GL JS documentation; the version line is the latest `maplibre-gl` published to the npm registry, read with `npm view`. Byte measurements on the comparison page are taken locally from this repository's pinned `maplibre-gl` dependency, not from this record.
records.comparability: A renderer engine and Honua's intended runtime partner, not a competitor in the headless-client category. Its operation cells describe what the renderer alone provides, which is exactly the gap Honua fills.

crs.note: renders in its own display projection

records.claim: Mapbox GL JS is a polished commercial web map SDK centered on the Map class and Mapbox Style Specification. It renders configured vector, raster, raster-array, DEM, GeoJSON, image, video, and model sources and provides projections, globe, terrain, and 3D styling, but it does not provide Honua-style arbitrary GIS endpoint discovery, cross-protocol capability negotiation, or semantic query planning.
records.methodology: Product scope and operation-level behavior read from Mapbox's official GL JS guides and API navigation; the version line is the latest `mapbox-gl` version read from the public npm registry on the observation date.
records.comparability: A vendor-integrated renderer SDK whose specialized web-service APIs remain separate. It compares directly with Honua plus a renderer on map-runtime developer experience, 3D, and lifecycle; it is not a like-for-like package-size comparison with the headless Honua client alone.

discovery.note: configured Mapbox/style sources, not arbitrary GIS service discovery

paging.note: renderer tile/source loading, not a typed feature paging client

edits.note: no first-party persistent feature edit transaction in GL JS

crs.note: display projections and globe; not a general source reprojection client

records.claim: CARTO's API client provides typed warehouse table, SQL query, tileset, H3, Quadbin, raster, and boundary data-source models that feed deck.gl layers and widget calculations. It is a direct SDK competitor in cloud-native spatial analytics, while remaining CARTO-platform-specific rather than an arbitrary open GIS endpoint client.
records.methodology: Data-source and query surface read from CARTO's official developer reference; the version line is the latest `@carto/api-client` version read from the public npm registry on the observation date.
records.comparability: A headless data/application client that delegates rendering to deck.gl and targets CARTO-managed warehouse APIs. It compares directly with Honua's Source, query-planning, columnar/tiled handoff, and warehouse roadmap, but not with Honua's open-protocol endpoint breadth. Deployment and licensing are platform-level comparisons outside this package-scoped record.

discovery.note: fetchMap enumerates layers for a known Builder map; no arbitrary service-root discovery

paging.note: getTable exposes limit, offset, and total; caller drives the page loop

edits.note: documented API-client data-source surface is read/visualization oriented

crs.note: no general CRS declaration, validation, or negotiation contract

capabilityNegotiation.note: typed source/warehouse contracts; no negotiated runtime capability document

planning.note: accepts SQL or named sources; no accepted-plan or explain result

lifecycle.note: fetchMap auto-refresh exposes stopAutoRefresh; no universal source disposal

records.claim: Felt's JavaScript SDK exposes a FeltController for embedded or in-product hosted maps, including viewport, layers, cursor-paged feature reads, selection, session-scoped layers and elements, drawing tools, UI panels and actions, filters, statistics, and events. It is a direct benchmark for hosted application coherence; SDK-created elements and GeoJSON layers are ephemeral and are not evidence of persisted collaborative authoring.
records.methodology: SDK model and public surface read from Felt's official getting-started guide and linked API reference; the version line is the latest `@feltmaps/js-sdk` version read from the public npm registry on the observation date.
records.comparability: A hosted application-control SDK, not a renderer-neutral service kernel. It compares directly on embedded-controller, layer, selection, UI, event, and session-scoped authoring developer experience; it does not compare directly on open-protocol discovery, general CRS or planning, persisted feature transactions, or self-hosted portability.

discovery.note: enumerates layers/entities inside a known Felt map; no endpoint discovery

paging.note: getFeatures returns page tokens; caller drives the loop

edits.note: no persisted feature transaction; SDK-created elements and GeoJSON layers are session-only

crs.note: no general projection/CRS contract in the JS SDK

rendering.note: embeds and controls the Felt-hosted renderer; renderer is outside the package

lifecycle.note: event APIs return unsubscribe functions; no documented controller/iframe dispose contract
